payload.body: ISSUE:0002 red, before the fix: d6408f1 adds renewal_write_keeps_claude_items_readable_by_security (ignored; CI still runs the old test). Reproduce: cargo test --locked --lib renewal_write_keeps_claude_items_readable_by_security -- --ignored. Output on rhadamanth: panicked at src/auth.rs:1012:5, 'partitions after the renewal write: ["cdhash:9dbfbfa21ae33cd8278abc0e0757b53168ec83a7"]'. Before that write the item's partitions were apple-tool: plus the test binary's own cdhash; ccusage's in-process write reset them to the writer's partition alone, so it fails on the partition assertion, not on access. Log: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Ccusage/e1e5d4f2-40c1-4c02-8b5f-93719b6fc69d/scratchpad/issue-0002/red.log. Research findings (Claude Code 2.1.317 binary, read-only, and experiments on disposable keychains). (1) Service: 'Claude Code' + OAUTH_FILE_SUFFIX + '-credentials' + '-' + the first 8 hex of sha256 over NFC(CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR) when set, else over NFC(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as given, unresolved); account: $USER, else os.userInfo().username, and claude-code-user when the name has a character outside [a-zA-Z0-9._-]; stdin limit: the whole security -i line, newline included, at most 4032 characters (security itself splits lines near 4096); exit 44 is errSecItemNotFound and 36 errSecInteractionNotAllowed; 2 s timeout per call. (2) A keychain created outside ~/Library/Keychains is version 256 with no partition list at all, so the fixture keychain lives in ~/Library/Keychains as ccusage-test-<pid>-<n>.keychain-db; create-keychain leaves the search list alone and the fixture is deleted on drop. (3) A write through security -i also resets the partitions to its writer's, apple-tool:, which is why writing through security keeps the items readable. (4) find-generic-password -w prints the password as hex when any byte is non-printing, eg a non-ASCII character in the JSON, so the reader decodes both. (5) security's stderr echoes the hex of a line it cannot parse, so ccusage never shows security's output. (6) There is no security command to add an app to an existing item's decrypt ACL, and the write path needs only the partition (the encrypt entry allows any app), so the test grants the partition alone. (7) Safety incident, contained: security -i add-generic-password with a keychain path that does not exist silently adds to the default keychain. My first experiment did that, putting one fake item (service ccusage-exp-51447, account fixture-user, one 0x00 byte) into hv's login keychain at 09:17Z by its own creation date. I deleted that exact item at once (lookup now exits 44). No real item was read or changed, and find-generic-password does not fall back. Every write since checks that its keychain file exists, and the fix's update-only lookup refuses before any write to a keychain that is not there. Next, the fix: /usr/bin/security for read and write, NFC service names (unicode-normalization, macOS only), and security-framework only as a macOS dev-dependency for the test. I carry on unless you say wait.
